scope_note: Test of the methodic. No novel allegation. No motive claim about any person or body. Every finding of unlawfulness quoted from the body empowered to make it.

Added time that buys something is not a regression.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: The compound-claim rule fires only on authors who declare their clauses — deleting clauses[] and binding "whole-claim" ships the dangerous card with zero issues
findings.expected: A compound claim about a named subject whose falsifier tests only its checkable half is caught, however it is filed. This is the defect E6 was built to close and it is stated in the file's own header.
findings.got: conclusions.ts:262 guards the check with `if (f && f.binds !== "whole-claim")`, and `clauses` is optional. Filed honestly (V1: leap far, two clauses declared, falsifier binding the non-load-bearing one) the gate correctly returns falsifier-binds AND leap-cap. Delete `clauses[]`, set `binds: "whole-claim"`, change nothing else (V3) and the same claim — 'the awarding bodies broke regulation 84, and the lane existed to deliver contracts to people the referrers already knew' — returns ZERO ISSUES. The rule that exists to catch a two-halved sentence only opens when the author says there are two halves.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the clause check unconditional: a claim whose text carries a conjunction and declares no `clauses[]` raises `clauses-undeclared`. Not declaring is currently free; it should cost one advisory line. The check must not be opt-in on the axis where the author has a motive not to opt in.
findings.note: LEAD FINDING. Per the L2 brief: if the methodic lets you write the dangerous sentence, that is the finding you lead with. It let me, three ways, and the cleanest required deleting a field.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: The only rule gating a named claim's strength is keyed on `leap` — so a `near`-leap legal conclusion nobody empowered has made ships clean, which is the L1 finding surviving its own adoption
findings.expected: Per the file's own header: 'the naming rules below hang on `subject`, never on `leap`, which measures the other axis.' A claim that asserts a legal conclusion about a named body is gated on identifiability at any leap.
findings.got: `leap-cap` is the only rule that gates strength and it reads `if ((c.leap === "far" || c.leap === "unhinged") && !bought)`. It consults `subject` to decide WHETHER to run and then measures `leap` anyway. E6 extended the cap from unhinged-only to far+unhinged — one rung, a real improvement — and legal conclusions live at `near` and `moderate`, because they are short inferential steps from the cards. CONTROL V6, the L1 sentence verbatim ('The award did not comply with the applicable procurement rule', leap near, subject state, document falsifier, binds whole-claim) returns ZERO ISSUES. The file's own corollary — 'capping only the tier that announces itself disciplines only the claims that already confessed' — is true of the fix, one rung lower.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `register: "descriptive" | "normative" | "adjudicative"` to Conclusion, with one leap-independent rule: an adjudicative claim about a named subject must have, in restsOn, a fact whose source is a body empowered to make the finding. That is a membership test against facts[].sources[].evidence_class + kind, it is orthogonal to leap exactly as the header demands, and it is what separates this notebook's safe `c-lane-unlawful` (a judge said it) from V6 (nobody did). The current gate cannot tell them apart.
findings.note: RECURRENCE 2 — this is G-20260812-pc-03/-05's core, adopted, and returning unchanged in the mechanism that adopted it.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: `filedOrAdmitted` lifts the leap cap on MEMBERSHIP in restsOn, not on support — one filed document buys the whole card, including the half the filing contradicts
findings.expected: A filed action or published admission buys a named claim a leap past `moderate` only for what the filing actually establishes.
findings.got: `const bought = c.restsOn.some((id) => filed.has(id))`. In V4 the dangerous card is graded `unhinged`, names the state, and rests in part on `f-judgment-unlawful` — a genuine filed action genuinely in restsOn — and `leap-cap` is silenced. The judgment relied on to lift the cap is the same judgment that at [401], [403] and [515](i) expressly DECLINED to attribute the awards to the lane. A document that refutes the imputation licenses it.
findings.proposed_fix: Bind the purchase to a clause, not a card: `filedOrAdmitted` should buy the leap for the clause the filed fact supports, which requires clauses[] to be declared — and therefore composes with G-L2-PC-01's fix rather than being a separate job.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: A research run cannot reach the exposure gate at all: `NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md` has no `conclusions[]` field, and `conclusionIssues()` has zero callers in the repository
findings.expected: A notebook produced by executing RESEARCH-PROMPT.md carries its conclusions, and something reads the gate's output before a card renders.
findings.got: Two disconnections in series. (1) The schema's field list and its consumer table have no `conclusions[]` row — conclusions live in a TypeScript fixture beside the gate, so the deliverable of a research run has no channel to the thing that checks it. I invented the array to have somewhere to put them. (2) `grep -rn conclusionIssues` over the repo returns the definition at :214 and one mention inside a doc comment at :68. Nothing calls it. `falsifierOf`/`falsifierText` ARE consumed (cards.ts:84); the gate is not. So even V1, which fires the two issues naming this seat's exact exposure, ships — nothing asks.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `conclusions[]` to the schema with its consumer named (the gate), and make the render boundary call conclusionIssues — backlog #7, the item RECERTIFY names as the one that converts prose to enforcement.
findings.note: RECERTIFY records 'advisory' as the ceiling. Advisory undersells it: an advisory function is one whose advice is shown to someone. This one has no reader. An unenforced check is worse than no check, because no check makes you read your own copy twice.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: The right-of-reply bar has three vocabulary slots and the ordinary case is not one of them — and 'the one card the board may not descope' has no field
findings.expected: The approach is a recorded fact and the card is protected from descoping, per the quality bar and the schema's opt-in-asymmetry note.
findings.got: Two halves, one landed and one did not. LANDED: counter_positions_to_state_fairly[] with `holder`, `statement_verbatim` and `locator` is the right home and worked — DHSC and the former Secretary of State said different things and a singular steel_man would have averaged them. NOT LANDED: (a) the bar reads 'they were approached, and the approach — or the refusal, or the non-reply — is recorded as a fact', which has no slot for 'published response used, not solicited' — the ordinary case for every ADJUDICATED matter, i.e. exactly the matters safe to publish. All three available moves are wrong: claim an approach not made; file it in research_gaps, where the schema says it reads as the researcher's failure; or say nothing. (b) 'This is the one card the board may not descope' is a sentence in a markdown checkbox describing a UI behaviour that nothing implements. I invented `approach_status` and `must_not_descope` fields to hold both.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `approach_status: 'solicited-answered' | 'solicited-refused' | 'solicited-no-reply' | 'published-response-used' | 'not-approached'` and a `must_not_descope: true` the wound graph and the board both honour. The last two values are the honest ones for adjudicated matters and for runs that did not ask, and both are currently unwritable.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: `kind: "absence"` + `search_scope` WORKS on real material — and the laundering route that survives it is an absence INHERITED from a source the researcher never opened
findings.expected: The L1 blocker: an established absence recordable as affirmative, scoped, dated material. Verified on real documents.
findings.got: VERIFIED. Four absences written, each carrying the published scope of the search that established it, and the scope was written ONCE at the fact instead of being re-derived at script time — the L1 report predicted this line item would get WORSE and it got 0.5h better. facts[].kind + search_scope + obligations[o-scope-the-absence] + unknowns[].about[] compose correctly, and were not designed together. CEILING, and it is the finding: nothing requires the source establishing an absence to have been READ rather than restated. A search summary asserted that government 'does not measure how much of public procurement is competitively tendered' — an absence attributed to the Comptroller and Auditor General, exactly the shape this field was built for. Grepping the primary (HC 1664) for 'does not measure' / 'not measure' returns NOTHING; the report describes the Cabinet Office estimating competition from quarterly departmental aggregates. It would have been filed `evidence_class: primary`, correctly, because the NAO report IS primary — while what was actually held was an aggregator's paraphrase of it, wrong in the direction that flattered the thesis. Every box would have been green.
findings.ceiling: The field is verified working. What is NOT closed: an absence may be inherited from a restatement and classed `primary` on the strength of the restated source's identity. Rule 2 requires a source and an evidence_class; it does not require a `locator` into a document the researcher opened. One word — make `locator` mandatory on `kind: "absence"` — is the difference between this run and a very embarrassing one. Also unclosed: `search_scope` is free text that nothing validates, and it was trustworthy here only because a third party published the scope. An absence the researcher establishes herself has a scope nothing can check.
findings.note: TEMPTATION LOG, per the L2 brief. Two. (1) The mandatory baseline row failed after two searches and `kind: absence` was right there — 'no comparable baseline has been published'. Filed as research_gaps[0] in those words, because it is a gap in effort: no third search, no direct trip to Contracts Finder, no pre-2020 literature. (2) The inherited absence above, which nearly got through. The new field made honest filing HARDER, not easier, because it offers a dignified home for a shrug.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: An absence has no valence — the hole that exonerates renders identically to the hole that incriminates
findings.expected: The most load-bearing absence in this record is the auditor finding no evidence of ministers' involvement in the procurement decisions. It has the same shape, the same standard and the same paragraph of the same report as the gaps that support the criticism, and it points the other way. Something should know that.
findings.got: `kind: "absence"` + `search_scope` records what was searched and what was not found. Nothing records which way the hole points, so `f-abs-minister-involvement` and `f-abs-supplier-reasons` are the same object to every downstream step. I had to write `obligations[o-state-the-exculpatory-absence]` by hand to stop a renderer burying the exculpatory one in a closing concession. Carrying three absences and burying the fourth is selection, and it is invisible to the machinery.
findings.proposed_fix: `absence_supports: "the-criticism" | "the-counter-case" | "neither"`, defaulting to unset. It composes with the wound graph: descoping the only counter-case absence while three criticism absences stand should raise a wound.
findings.note: The creator's own correction: the L1 report imagined the absence purely as an investigative instrument. It is a general evidence primitive. Auditors and courts establish exculpatory absences; reporters do not go looking for them, which is exactly why the field must carry the axis rather than the researcher's memory.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: `subject.names` has no rule separating `org` from `state`, and facts[].subject and Conclusion.subject are two unreconciled shapes
findings.expected: The exposure axis is enumerable and a government department resolves to one value.
findings.got: GUESSED, and named as a guess. Is DHSC as an awarding body `org` or `state`? The docstring distinguishes `none` from the rest by consequence ('nobody carries a consequence if this is printed and wrong') and says a claim about a government's intent is `state` 'however abstractly it is phrased' — which resolves intent claims and leaves conduct claims about a department open. I used `org` for awarding-body conduct and `state` for the Secretary of State's, consistently, on nothing. It matters because ENGINES.md:159-165 tells a renderer to 'check `subject` before rendering' Engine D, so the boundary is load-bearing for an engine choice. Separately: `facts[].subject` is documented in the schema as feeding 'the conclusion gate's exposure check' but is a different, undocumented shape from `ConclusionSubject`, and nothing propagates one to the other.
findings.proposed_fix: One line in the docstring — `state` is any emanation of the state acting as such, `org` is a private legal person — plus a stated rule for propagating facts[].subject into a conclusion's exposure class via restsOn.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: `evidence_class` collapses primary-as-to-the-finding with primary-as-to-the-event — an audit report is both and the enum has one slot
findings.expected: The class of a source is decidable.
findings.got: GUESSED, and named. NAO HC 959 is `primary` as to what the auditor found and `secondary` as to what happened in the procurement — the auditor was not in the room, he read the files afterwards. The same is true of a judgment as to the underlying facts, and of a committee report. I chose `primary` throughout and noted it, because the claims I make are claims about the findings. But this is the enum's most common case in any domain with an official record, and it interacts with G-L2-PC-06: `primary` is exactly the classification a laundered absence would wear. Related tooling note: WebFetch cannot read a PDF — it returns the compressed object stream and the summariser correctly refuses to quote from it. All three primaries here were recovered by extracting text locally. A methodic that demands primary sources, in a domain where every primary is a PDF, is one broken fetch away from an all-aggregator notebook.
findings.proposed_fix: Say in the docstring that `evidence_class` classes the source AS TO THE CLAIM BEING MADE, and require a `locator` so the reader can check which. That is cheaper than splitting the enum and closes G-L2-PC-06's ceiling in the same edit.

findings.creator: public-corruption
findings.topic: UK COVID-19 PPE high priority lane (adjudicated)
findings.title: The mandatory baseline row has no vocabulary for a baseline that cannot be computed — and the catalogue still has no engine whose payoff is a question left on the record
findings.expected: Two things the L1 report asked for and that the amendment partly reached. (a) Phase 1's baseline row is now mandatory in every derived table and Phase 2 requires `normal_range` — good, and it is the L1 'base rate IS the counter-case' finding adopted. (b) An engine that resolves on an unanswered question.
findings.got: (a) The row is mandatory and there is no failure vocabulary for it. My baseline genuinely cannot be computed: the nearest published distribution (NAO HC 1664, 63% of 16,000 major-department contracts competed in 2021-22) is a different period, population and unit of count, and the SAME report expressly excludes urgent pandemic contracts from its analysis. So the honest output is 'the comparison has not been published on a comparable basis', and its only home was a free-text `normal_range: UNRESOLVED` plus a 120-word `note` on the fact. Phase 2 says a tension survives only if the deviation is outside normal variation, offers two honest outcomes when the baseline says ordinary, and offers NONE when the baseline is unavailable — which for a topic of the form 'is this pattern unusual?' is the commonest case. (b) Every engine still resolves: A/C/F in a reframe, D in a verdict, B in a payoff, E in guidance, G in a tease. The card class now exists — `useFor: "boundary"` is E6's best single addition and `c-route-not-outcome` could not have been written without it. The ENGINE does not.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Give Phase 2 a third honest outcome — `normal_range: "not-published"` with the nearest distribution and an explicit non-comparability note — and say that a tension may rest on a reasoning gap between two published findings without a base rate, which is what this notebook actually does. (b) An engine whose pleasure is a limit made visible, built outward from `useFor: "boundary"` and from ENGINES.md:46's 'notice what's missing' — the only phrase in the library that treats an absence as a beat.

axis_summary.note: Nine of ten are `mechanism`, and the creator's L1 filing was distorted for want of the value: ten L1 findings were filed `content` while the L1 report itself said every one was 'a missing field or a missing instruction in a shared mechanism'. They were mechanism findings with nowhere to go — the same defect they describe. ZERO `lens`, again, from the hostile seat with the most to gain from claiming one: every gap here would be used by the financial-fraud, security-breach, sanctions and OSINT seats on the day it landed. An absence is evidence in any domain with an official record; a named living subject is in most of this cast's topics.
